title: B Major Piano Chord (B): Notes, Inversions & PDF
description: Learn B major on piano with B, D-sharp and F-sharp. Read its bass notes and inversions, try the note exercise and print the reference.
user_task: Locate this exact triad and compare its three bass positions.
questions: Is the B major chord all black keys?
What is the difference between B and Bm?
Why do the inversion examples jump down in register?
Can C-flat major be replaced with B in written music?

blocks.heading: Notes and keyboard position
blocks.body: B major consists of B, D-sharp and F-sharp. The chord has a white-key root and two black-key chord tones. The displayed root-position example is B4–D♯5–F♯5. Numbers after note letters identify octaves, not fingers. Use the diagram, note list and bass label together; Play chord sounds the selected notes together, while the note-by-note control sounds them from low to high.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] rules; [推断] register and original teaching example

blocks.heading: What to notice
blocks.body: Read both sharp signs. Using D natural changes the third and produces B minor when F-sharp stays fixed. Using F natural changes the fifth as well. The symbol B is not an instruction to use only white keys. From B, the major third is D-sharp and the perfect fifth is F-sharp. Their distances are four and seven semitones above the root. In B/D♯, D-sharp becomes the bass, but it does not replace B as the root.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original explanation from preserved note data and cited rules

blocks.heading: Compare three positions
blocks.body: Read each bass note before selecting a position. The root-position example starts with B; first inversion starts with D♯; second inversion starts with F♯. The chord tones stay the same. These are independently chosen reference registers, not an ascending exercise. Switching a position must update the selected note order, diagram, sound and current-print snapshot together. Hand numbers, when available, apply only to the root example.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] derived inversion explanation; controls are implementation acceptance requirements
